A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same bounded adaptive clipping work. Their main text, equations, tables, figures, and complete appendices are readable and support comparison, despite some internal reporting inconsistencies.

before.justification: v1 reports original mean-estimation experiments and private image/tabular classification results on four datasets, including hyperparameter analyses in Appendix B.

after.justification: v2 reports original experiments on five datasets, including CelebA, expanded baseline comparisons, sensitivity studies, and training-trajectory analyses.

M1.justification: Algorithm 2 retains the normalized gradient update, noisy gradient-count query, exponential clipping-bound adaptation, and lower-bound constraint. The newly evaluated fixed CLB = 0.1 variant uses an existing parameter setting; it introduces no new clipping component or update rule.

E1.justification: v2 retains the four original datasets and adds CelebA eyeglasses classification with gender-specific evaluation (Section 4.1, Figure 3). This extends coverage from handwritten digits, clothing, and census records to natural face images and demographic disparities in attribute prediction.

E2.justification: v2 adds AUTO to the retained image and tabular comparisons, including DP-HPO experiments. Appendix C.1 additionally evaluates FairDP against the existing methods on Adult and Dutch using group accuracy and demographic parity. Constant and unbounded adaptive clipping remain.

E3.justification: v2 adds demographic-parity evaluation and fixed-lower-bound controls. The tabular privacy-budget set changes from {0.1, 0.2, 0.5} to {0.05, 0.1, 0.2}, and AUTO receives a tabular learning-rate grid extending to 50 (Table A3). DP-HPO curves also use different reported total privacy budgets, preventing direct same-budget performance comparisons.

E4.justification: Beyond v1's illustrative trajectories and hyperparameter heatmaps, v2 adds an Adult accuracy-sensitivity analysis (Figure A1), tests fixed CLB = 0.1 against tuning (Appendix C.2), and adds Skewed MNIST/CelebA training trajectories (C.4). Appendix C.3 also expands micro-versus-macro accuracy analysis beyond the earlier Skewed MNIST heatmaps.

E5.justification: The reported DP-HPO averaging decreases from 20 runs in v1 Figure 4 to 10 runs in v2 Figure 5. Standard-error reporting and ten-run optimal-hyperparameter comparisons remain. Table A1 clarifies the tuning summaries as ten random seeds with twenty trials per tuning run.

E6.justification: Retained numerical results are revised: bounded clipping's Skewed MNIST ResNet-18 macro/worst-class accuracy at epsilon = 2 changes from 94.32%/71.41% in v1 Table 5 to 94.11%/68.87% in v2 Table A4. v2 also adds CelebA, AUTO, FairDP, fixed-bound, and demographic-parity results. DP-HPO curves change, although conflicting endpoint budgets in v2 Figure 5 and Table A7 limit their interpretation.

T1.justification: Lemma 3.1 expands Gaussian-mechanism composition from unit sensitivities to arbitrary sensitivities Delta1 and Delta2, retaining the original formula as a special case. The applied privacy theorem remains unchanged, and no substantial new proof development is added.

C1.justification: The central failure-mode diagnosis and lower-bound remedy remain. v2 adds an abstract claim of a seven-percentage-point worst-class advantage over AUTO and makes empirical Pareto-frontier membership a conclusion claim, refining v1's broader assertions of outperforming existing methods.

C2.justification: v2 adds regime-dependent bias–variance explanations, discusses when small clipping bounds can help, and explains AUTO's advantage with very limited tuning trials. It distinguishes demographic parity from predictive accuracy and explicitly identifies tuning overhead as a limitation. The conclusion also replaces v1's assertion that DP inherently enforces unfairness with a more qualified distinction between privacy guarantees and accuracy disparities.

D1.justification: v1 promises a future code release; v2 supplies a repository link. v2 newly identifies the BoTorch sampler, AUTO's stability constant, and model-specific runtimes, including revised tabular timing. Conversely, v1's explicit gender-balancing statement for Adult/Dutch is omitted; this changes documentation without establishing an actual preprocessing change.

R1.justification: v2 substantially broadens positioning through AUTO and FairDP comparisons and reconciles its findings with prior small-clipping results using bias–variance reasoning. New discussion cites Rehn et al. (2026), Barocas et al. (2023), and Defrance and De Bie (2025) to contextualize clipping regimes and fairness trade-offs.

P1.justification: v2 reorganizes Methodology, moves dataset preprocessing from Appendix A into Section 4.1, restructures the experimental appendices, and substantially rewrites results discussion and conclusion. Terminology shifts throughout toward disparate impact and accuracy parity, while algorithms gain explanatory annotations.

P2.justification: The principal accuracy-versus-budget line plots are redesigned as joint-performance scatter panels, with expanded line-plot comparisons appearing in the appendix. v2 adds CelebA, demographic-parity, sensitivity, and trajectory displays, expands result tables, and revises heatmap captions and axes. The journal layout also replaces the earlier wrapped figures and algorithms.

improvement.justification: v2 substantially strengthens validation through alternative clipping/fairness baselines, demographic-parity evaluation, CelebA, and direct tests of tuning sensitivity and a fixed lower bound. These address important gaps in v1's comparative evidence and practical tuning claims. Reporting weaknesses temper the gains: DP-HPO uses fewer runs, and Figure 5's Fashion-MNIST endpoint epsilon = 116.8 conflicts with Table A7's 13.370. Nevertheless, the broader comparative and diagnostic evidence provides a substantial net improvement.
